study_identification.title: Transdiagnostic dimensions of psychopathology explain individuals' unique deviations from normative neurodevelopment in brain structure

study_characteristics.study_objective: To build normative models of cortical volume development in youth and test whether individual deviations from normative neurodevelopment better predict transdiagnostic psychopathology dimensions than raw cortical volume; and to assess whether overall psychopathology accounts for disorder-general neuroanatomical abnormalities compared to disorder-specific effects.

deviation_metric.reason: Deviations are Z-scores computed per region from the normative model; regional averages used for ROIs; deviations reduced via PCA for prediction.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: Deviations (Z) were modeled in the remaining 990 individuals (test, ) and paired with six dimensions of psychopathology.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Ridge regression with 100x 10-fold cross-validation predicting six psychopathology dimensions from PCs of deviation maps; nuisance covariates (age, sex) regressed from targets within folds; significance by permutation (100,000). Regional correlations between deviations and overall psychopathology in vmPFC/mOFC, inferior temporal, dACC, and insula; case–control comparisons of deviations for ADHD and depression, with overlap reduced after controlling for overall psychopathology.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Patterns of deviations from normative neurodevelopment predict transdiagnostic psychopathology better than raw cortical volume; overall psychopathology is associated with deviations in vmPFC/mOFC, inferior temporal, and dACC; ADHD and depression exhibit overlapping deviation patterns that diminish when accounting for overall psychopathology.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Multivariate deviations yielded improved out-of-sample prediction of psychopathology dimensions compared to raw cortical volume. Correlations between overall psychopathology and deviations in ventromedial prefrontal, inferior temporal, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortices were stronger than those observed for specific dimensions. Conventional case–control comparisons of deviations in depression and ADHD showed spatially overlapping effects that diminished when controlling for overall psychopathology.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Single-site cohort without external domain validation; modeling focused on cortical volume with parcellated ROIs; specific normative modeling algorithm and software are not explicitly described, limiting reproducibility assessment.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Sex-specific age trajectories were modeled; deviations reduced via PCA with most predictive signal in PC1; sensitivity analyses using alternative parcellation (Lausanne463) and assessment of potential confounds (IQ, T1 QA, T1 SNR).

general_notes.general_notes: Final sample: 1,271 participants after exclusions; normative model trained on 281 HC and applied to 990 remaining participants. Single 3T Siemens Tim Trio site; structural preprocessing via ANTs with custom adolescent template.
